title: Senior's toolkit: the pipeline
summary: The pipeline commands and switches people who live in PowerShell use every day, and when to reach for each.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the pipeline
steps.body: These are the commands an experienced PowerShell user types without thinking. Each one replaces a loop you would otherwise write by hand.

toolkit.what: Shows an object's type, properties and methods. The first thing to run on anything unfamiliar.
flags: filter member names with a wildcard

toolkit.what: Every property and its value for one object: what the default table view hides.
flags: all properties, not just the view's
with error records: show the hidden details too

toolkit.what: Picks properties (or builds calculated ones), or the first, last or unique objects.
flags: slice the stream (and -First stops the upstream early)
output the plain values, not objects
toolkit.example: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 FullName, @{ n = 'MB'; e = { [math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1) } }

toolkit.what: Keeps objects that match. Short form for one condition, a script block for more.
flags: the short form: property, operator, value
a script block for several conditions

toolkit.what: Sorts by one or more properties or expressions, typed as they are.
flags: sort by an expression (cast strings from CSV)
the first or last N after sorting (PowerShell 7)

toolkit.what: Counts or collects objects by a property value.
flags: a lookup table: value to its objects
toolkit.example: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 500 | Group-Object ProviderName -NoElement | Sort-Object Count -Descending

toolkit.what: Count, sum, average, minimum and maximum of a property.
flags: all of them, plus standard deviation

toolkit.what: Runs a script block per object; `-Begin`/`-End` run once around them.
flags: shortest form: `ForEach-Object Name` reads or calls a member

steps.prompt: Match each switch to what it does.
pairs: a numeric sort on a text column

steps.prompt: Why should `Format-Table` (and `Format-List`) only ever be the **last** command in a pipeline?
options: They output formatting instructions, not your objects, so any command after them gets garbage
They are slow on large inputs
They only work in the console, not in scripts
They change the original objects' properties
steps.explain: Format-* cmdlets emit internal format objects (their type names start with `Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Internal.Format`). Piping those into `Export-Csv` or `Where-Object` gives nonsense. Filter, sort and select first; format only for the screen. The boss has exactly this bug.

steps.prompt: The ten oldest files under `D:\Exports`, oldest first, with their age in days.
steps.explain: `-File` skips folders. `Sort-Object LastWriteTime` is oldest first by default, so `-First 10` takes the oldest. Subtracting two dates gives a `TimeSpan`, and `.Days` is its whole days.
Strings sort as text, character by character: `'1'` comes before `'9'`. Numbers sort as numbers. Everything from `Import-Csv`, `Get-Content` and most REST APIs starts as a string.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Run `Get-Member` before you guess a property name, filter as early as you can (ideally with the first command's own `-Filter`), and keep `Format-*` for the very end of a line you are reading on screen. When a number sorts strangely, check its type: `$x.GetType().Name`.
